summary: Iteration 14 — KB consolidation / learned-knowledge review. Backend pytest (tests/test_iteration_14.py, 4 tests): 3 pass, 1 fail. Frontend UI verified for both offenses. Also detected + fixed a critical environment corruption: /app/backend/llm_engine.py was left as the test_llm_mssp.py mock stub and /app/backend/llm_engine_orig.py was missing, causing every background LLM job to raise 'No module named llm_engine_orig' and settings.llm.analysis_mode was 'kb' — restored real llm_engine.py via git checkout, flipped settings.llm.analysis_mode=llm & enable_llm=true, restarted backend, LLM jobs now run to completion in ~90s. PASS: (1) 00316 Outbound instant kb-template report → mssp_report_source=kb-template, kb_learning={ticket_count:6, match_score:100, verdict_counts:{TP:6}, alert_name set}, analysis contains src 10.13.122.218 and dst 162.159.134.233, recs include 'Block ... 162.159.134.233' and 'Investigate ... 10.13.122.218', NO review-logs pointer, NO 'USB' sentence (consensus filtering worked). (2) 00317 Inbound → mssp_report_source=rule-engine (NOT kb-template), kb_learning absent — fuzzy Inbound-vs-Outbound / UC-number penalty correctly rejects the 00316 KB. (3) PowerShell single-row KB → kb_learning.ticket_count=1, recs grounded with powershell.exe/outlook.exe; after LLM completes impact_lines contain no imperative Block/Isolate/Collect and no Report:/Type: Critical/Critical Severity: junk. FAIL: (2) 00316 Outbound after LLM completes — mssp_report_source=llm, generated_by=llm:Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, kb_learning.ticket_count=6, verdict=TP, verdict_reason grounded, impact non-empty, no review-logs pointer — BUT LLM output is NOT grounded in the offense's own artifacts: analysis bullets are generic ('The Incident Alert was triggered due to an outbound connection…') with 0 mentions of 10.13.122.218 or 162.159.134.233, and recommendations #1-#4 use the generic form 'Block the External IP:', 'Investigate the Source Host for Malware or Beaconing:', 'Review Proxy and DNS Logs:', 'Validate the CTI Feed Match and Update Blocklists:' — NONE contain the actual IPs — while rec #5 is the echoed-artifact line 'Destination IP: 162.159.134.233' (exactly the kind of leak the review says must not appear). A previous run of the same offense additionally produced analysis line #1 saying '…involves an inbound connection…' (use case is outbound — direction contradiction) and rec junk bullets 'Port Number: 443', 'User-Agent: Not specified', 'Proxy Server: Zscaler', 'DNS Server: 172.20.2.36' — LLM outputs are non-deterministic across runs but the underlying grounding/routing/direction bugs reproduce. Frontend: 00316 mssp report tab shows testids offense-mssp-report-source='Local LLM' + offense-mssp-report-kb-learning='KB · 6 tickets · 100%' + offense-mssp-report-verdict='TP', payload grid renders src/dst IPs, log source 'Zscaler Nanolog Streaming Service NSS@ 172.20.2.36', no 'Review the Zscaler…' pointer in DOM. 00317 mssp report tab shows Rule Engine badge and NO -kb-learning badge (locator count == 0), matches spec.

critical.issue: LLM analysis_lines are ungrounded — 0 bullets contain the offense's src IP 10.13.122.218 or dst IP 162.159.134.233 even though those IPs are in mssp_report.source_ip / destination_ip. _lead_bullet grounding and per-section LLM prompts appear to not be injecting THIS offense's artifacts into the LLM system prompt (or the grounding-repair pass is dropping them).

LLM recommendations #1-#4 (Block/Investigate/Review/Validate) all lack the concrete artifact — e.g. 'Block the External IP:' with no IP. The kb-template pre-report grounds these correctly (Block ... 162.159.134.233 / Investigate ... 10.13.122.218) but the LLM stage regresses them to generic sentences.

Echoed artifact line leaked into recommendations: 'Destination IP: 162.159.134.233'. _sanitize_bullets / _IMPERATIVE_RE routing must drop 'Key: value' echo bullets from the recommendations section (also seen in a prior run: 'Port Number: 443', 'User-Agent: Not specified', 'Proxy Server: Zscaler', 'DNS Server: 172.20.2.36').

Direction contradiction observed in one run: analysis bullet #1 read 'The use case involves an inbound connection from an external IP…' for an Outbound use case. fix_direction should catch and rewrite 'inbound' → 'outbound' when the offense's use-case direction is Outbound (matches review requirement 'no analysis bullet says inbound').

minor.issue: /app/backend/llm_engine.py had been overwritten by the test_llm_mssp.py mock stub in a previous pytest run and /app/backend/llm_engine_orig.py was missing, causing every background LLM job to error with 'No module named llm_engine_orig' and llm_status='failed'. The review already flagged the reverse (leftover llm_engine_orig.py) but the failure mode here was the opposite. Restored via `git checkout backend/llm_engine.py`. Recommend hardening test_llm_mssp.py teardown (or moving the module-swap into an isolated importlib-mock) so a failed teardown cannot leave the real backend broken.

settings.llm.analysis_mode was 'kb' and enable_llm was false in the running preview — LLM refinement wouldn't fire for any offense. Flipped to 'llm'/true for this test run; main agent should confirm the intended default and add a settings-migration or health-check.

critical_code_review_comments: llm_engine.py::build_llm_mssp_report_oneshot — per-section LLM prompts and _lead_bullet grounding must inject the offense's src_ip/dst_ip/host/user/process/port so bullet #1 is anchored to THIS offense; the current output is a use-case template with no artifact substitution.

llm_engine.py::_sanitize_bullets / _IMPERATIVE_RE — must drop 'Key: value' echoed lines (Destination IP:, Port Number:, User-Agent:, Proxy Server:, DNS Server:) from recommendations (route to fields grid instead).
kb_template.py::fix_direction — direction correction is either not being called on LLM output or is missing the 'inbound' → 'outbound' rewrite when use_case_direction='Outbound'.

tests/test_llm_mssp.py — file-swap fixture is fragile: if pytest is killed mid-run it leaves the backend importing a non-existent llm_engine_orig. Prefer monkeypatch of the module-level symbols or a sys.modules override.
action_items: Fix LLM grounding so analysis_lines and recommendations contain the offense's actual IPs/host/user/process (currently 0/N grounded for 00316 Outbound).
Filter echoed 'Key: value' bullets out of recommendations (Destination IP:, Port Number:, User-Agent:, Proxy Server:, DNS Server:).
Ensure fix_direction rewrites 'inbound' → 'outbound' (and vice-versa) on LLM output when use-case direction is known.
Harden test_llm_mssp.py teardown so a botched run cannot leave llm_engine.py as the mock stub / delete llm_engine_orig.py — this bricks background LLM investigations preview-wide.

context_for_next_testing_agent: 1) Real backend llm_engine.py must exist (785 lines, docstring starts 'Local-LLM driven MSSP L1 report generation.') — if you see a 35-line 'TEST MOCK' stub, git checkout backend/llm_engine.py and restart backend. 2) Settings.llm.analysis_mode must be 'llm' + enable_llm=true for the LLM refinement path; otherwise mssp_report_source stays 'kb-template' forever. 3) test_iteration_14.py's LLM test can drift due to LLM non-determinism — the failing assertion (grounded_total>=2) is the stable one; the direction/echoed-artifact leaks reproduce intermittently. 4) LLM investigate takes ~90-160s on this CPU; single-worker background queue.
rca of the issue: Root cause of 'LLM never completes' failure was environmental, not iteration-14 code: a previous test run of tests/test_llm_mssp.py left /app/backend/llm_engine.py as its 35-line TEST MOCK (docstring 'TEST MOCK — swapped in by test_llm_mssp.py to avoid downloading the real 3B LLM.') and its teardown deleted /app/backend/llm_engine_orig.py (the copy of the real module the mock imports). Every background LLM job therefore raised 'No module named llm_engine_orig' → llm_status='failed' → mssp_report_source stayed at kb-template. Restored the real 785-line llm_engine.py via `git checkout backend/llm_engine.py`, restarted backend, LLM jobs now complete. Root cause of the remaining pytest failure is a real product bug: build_llm_mssp_report_oneshot's per-section prompts and _lead_bullet grounding are not substituting THIS offense's IPs/host/user into the LLM output; the kb-template pre-report grounds correctly but the LLM stage regresses to a generic use-case template and additionally leaks 'Destination IP: 162.159.134.233' as a recommendation bullet (also 'Port Number: 443' etc. seen in a prior run) — the _IMPERATIVE_RE / _sanitize_bullets routing lets these Key:value lines through into recommendations.
